why: Telemetry for the corpus's first self-clearing case, derived from the numbers the incident text states. Every series here declares `hold: 4`, and that is the point of the case rather than a detail of it: the corpus could previously say 'the level change lasts the whole post-window' (`step`) or 'it lasts exactly one sample' (`spike`), and nothing in between, so every case sustained all eight post-onset samples and G3's sample axis could not refuse anything at any line. Four is not a chosen number -- it is the shortest hold at which both of G4's baselines still place the answer, because the robust baseline reads the post-window's median and four elevated samples in eight put that median between the two levels, where three leave it on the baseline. The control series is flat and exact: a burst that is slow without being down is the claim the case makes, and an error ratio that wobbled would contradict it.

series.quote: sat at 98% utilisation, up from its usual 12%
series.why: the saturation itself: the metric the burst moves, and the one a reader has to look at to call this `cpu-saturation` rather than `network-delay`. The baseline is well below the peak on purpose -- 0.98 with a 2 % jitter arm reaches 0.9996 and the unit's ceiling clamp then keeps it at 0.98..1, so the peak is a reading the scale can hold.
the effect the pager saw, and the case's SLI: a duration, so the RCA-eval exporters publish it as the latency column rather than skipping the case for having no latency to observe
the same four minutes one hop out. It is a symptom rather than a second fault, which is why the causal chain crosses this service instead of starting at it

series.quote: The storefront error ratio did not move
series.why: the control. A ratio of counted requests is a computation rather than a sample, so it is exact -- and it reads zero at both ends, which is what makes 'slow' and 'down' two different verdicts on this case rather than two words for one

noLogs: the text quotes a pager, three numbers and a duration, and no line any process wrote: the merge finished, which is the one kind of incident a log file records as nothing at all.
noTraces: the exchange the ticket measured is a query the storefront made and catalog-service waited on, and the text gives a percentile for it rather than a single span's duration, so a trace here would be a number this case invented rather than one it was annotated from.
